Louisiana Tech Bulldogs.status: Returning — the guide treats him as the quarterback whose running held last season's offense together.
Louisiana Tech Bulldogs.career_experience: Not addressed in guide as a career summary.
Louisiana Tech Bulldogs.passing: Not addressed individually; the guide reports Louisiana Tech's quarterbacks collectively posted an 8-to-9 touchdown-to-interception ratio while the team completed over 62% of its passes.
Louisiana Tech Bulldogs.rushing: Better than six yards per carry — the guide argues things could have gone very differently without his running.
Louisiana Tech Bulldogs.efficiency: Team-level: over 62% completions from the quarterback group.
Louisiana Tech Bulldogs.turnovers: He threw more interceptions than touchdowns; the group ratio was 8 to 9.
Louisiana Tech Bulldogs.author_confidence: Sceptical of the offense as a whole rather than of him individually. The guide's answer to whether to buy stock in the offense is built on concentration risk.
Louisiana Tech Bulldogs.positive_case: His running was the load-bearing element — better than six yards per carry — in an offense that finally carried its weight.
Louisiana Tech Bulldogs.concerns: A negative touchdown-to-interception ratio, and an offense whose rushing profile came from very few games: almost 11 yards per carry against Sam Houston, 5.9 against Liberty and 7.6 against Missouri State, rendered as 353 rushing yards against New Mexico State, 426 against Sam Houston, 319 against Liberty and 388 against Missouri State — four games accounting for 1,486 of 2,540 rushing yards, leaving just 1,054 across the other nine.
Louisiana Tech Bulldogs.supporting_cast: Not addressed in guide in detail beyond the rushing profile above.
Louisiana Tech Bulldogs.portal_context: Not addressed in guide at quarterback.
Louisiana Tech Bulldogs.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 5.5 wins, available at plus money, from a team that produced 3, 3 and 5 regular-season wins for Cumbie before last season's 7-5 mark. Its projection is 5.76 wins, above the number, but it calls the defense very ripe for regression and says the abundance of closely lined games makes that a prominent factor — Louisiana Tech is favoured by more than two points only three times.
Louisiana Tech Bulldogs.outlook_dependency: Moderate. The guide's Under is argued from defensive regression, the conference step up and personnel losses; the quarterback appears mainly as the reason last season's rushing worked.
Louisiana Tech Bulldogs.conflicts: The guide's rushing passage names three opponents by yards-per-carry then lists four by total rushing yards, adding New Mexico State. Both formulations are reproduced in the Team Database as printed and neither is corrected here.

Marshall Thundering Herd.status: Returning starter — the guide records him finding a home after bouncing around.
Marshall Thundering Herd.career_experience: First crack as a starter last season after stops at Florida and Syracuse.
Marshall Thundering Herd.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a count.
Marshall Thundering Herd.passing: Threw for more than 2,000 yards, accounting for 23 total touchdowns.
Marshall Thundering Herd.rushing: Led the team in rushing with 661 yards.
Marshall Thundering Herd.efficiency: Not addressed in guide as a rate; the guide notes team-level gains in yardage per game and completions.
Marshall Thundering Herd.turnovers: Not addressed in guide individually; Marshall posted a +6 turnover margin.
Marshall Thundering Herd.competition: None described — Del Rio-Wilson is the settled starter.
Marshall Thundering Herd.author_confidence: Positive and conditional on health. The guide says that if he stays healthy he should be fine.
Marshall Thundering Herd.positive_case: He took advantage of his first starting opportunity, leading the team in rushing while throwing for over 2,000 yards and accounting for 23 total touchdowns, in an offense that was nearly as good as the year before despite the coaching upheaval.
Marshall Thundering Herd.concerns: The supporting cast is the open question — running back was a committee approach and three backs who averaged 5-plus yards per carry are gone, as is leading receiver Demarcus Lacey, who had 28 more receptions than anyone else.
Marshall Thundering Herd.supporting_cast: Weakened but partly rebuilt. Receiver was a focal point in the portal and tight end Toby Payne is rated one of the best in the conference at his position.
Marshall Thundering Herd.portal_context: A 5-7 team did not really improve through the portal or the freshman class, judged by conference ranking, though receiver and cornerback were focal points.
Marshall Thundering Herd.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 7.5 wins, explicitly labelled not a bet but a gamble on the schedule. The favourable half: Marshall draws South Alabama and UL Monroe from the West and all conference home games are winnable. The unfavourable half: daunting road games at Penn State, James Madison and Old Dominion. It adds a specific warning about Ryan Beard, who put 474 yards on the Herd last season. Projection is 7.35 wins.
Marshall Thundering Herd.outlook_dependency: Moderate. The quarterback is treated as a settled strength; the guide's Under is a schedule position.

Old Dominion Monarchs.status: New starter, identity undetermined — Colton Joseph has gone to Wisconsin and the guide poses the succession as an open question.
Old Dominion Monarchs.previous_school: Jaxon Potter comes from Washington State; Quinn Henicle is the holdover.
Old Dominion Monarchs.career_experience: Henicle is the holdover who knows the system; Potter was the higher-graded recruit.
Old Dominion Monarchs.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as counts.
Old Dominion Monarchs.passing: Henicle completed only 42.5% of his passes and was 11-for-25 against a skeleton-crew USF team in the bowl game. Potter's production is not addressed.
Old Dominion Monarchs.rushing: Henicle ran for 4.8 yards per carry on 44 attempts.
Old Dominion Monarchs.competition: Genuinely open, and the guide weighs continuity against upside without choosing. In Henicle's favour it notes he was recruited by FCS schools with good rushing attacks and by Army, so he was clearly seen as an impact runner at the position.
Old Dominion Monarchs.backup: The two named candidates are Quinn Henicle and Jaxon Potter.
Old Dominion Monarchs.author_confidence: Low, with urgency attached. Its verdict is that neither looks poised to top Joseph's numbers, and Rahne needs to get this right and fix it early in the season if he has not settled it coming out of camp.
Old Dominion Monarchs.positive_case: Henicle knows the system and was viewed as an impact runner; Potter was the higher-graded recruit and was willing to cross the country as a California native.
Old Dominion Monarchs.concerns: Henicle was not very good, and the guide says plainly neither looks poised to match the departing starter, who rushed for more than 1,000 yards and threw for over 2,600.
Old Dominion Monarchs.scheme_fit: Kody Cook is promoted to offensive coordinator after coaching wide receivers, and also takes the quarterbacks; the guide calls him the logical promotion after Kevin Decker's departure for Memphis.
Old Dominion Monarchs.supporting_cast: Concentrated losses at receiver: only three players had 11-plus catches, posting 762, 719 and 667 yards while nobody else exceeded 200 — and all three are gone. The guide expects a run-heavy team again, listing Devin Roche at 5.7 yards per carry and JUCO transfer Trey Hall, originally an Ole Miss commit.
Old Dominion Monarchs.portal_context: Colton Joseph left for Wisconsin and coordinator Kevin Decker for Memphis; Jaxon Potter and Trey Hall arrived. The guide generalises this into a structural observation about the Group of Six era: whiplash seasons are very possible now because of the portal.
Old Dominion Monarchs.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 7.5 wins, resting almost entirely on the schedule being kind to Rahne — James Madison and Marshall both come to Norfolk, the UConn road game is very winnable, and drawing Southern Miss and Louisiana Tech from the West is favourable. Its arithmetic: ODU is favoured in nine games and within +1.5 and +0.5 in two more, giving a projection of 7.51 wins.
Old Dominion Monarchs.outlook_dependency: High as a risk, low as a stated basis. The guide's Over rests on schedule, while naming the quarterback as the thing Rahne must fix early.
Old Dominion Monarchs.conflicts: The guide names two candidates and declines to state an expected starter, so this record carries no VSiN preseason expectation for the position.

South Alabama Jaguars.status: Returning starter — the guide notes he prepared all summer knowing the team is his.
South Alabama Jaguars.career_experience: Took over after Gio Lopez left for North Carolina following spring practices.
South Alabama Jaguars.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a count.
South Alabama Jaguars.passing: Completed 68% of his passes, 12th nationally as a team figure, with a 12-to-6 touchdown-to-interception ratio.
South Alabama Jaguars.efficiency: 68% completions, 12th nationally as a team figure.
South Alabama Jaguars.competition: None described — Davenport is the settled starter.
South Alabama Jaguars.author_confidence: Positive. Asked whether the offense improves, the guide's stated answer, with Applewhite calling plays, is yes.
South Alabama Jaguars.positive_case: A high completion rate with a positive touchdown-to-interception ratio, a full summer of preparation as the settled starter, and the head coach taking over play-calling.
South Alabama Jaguars.concerns: Modest rushing efficiency — 116 carries for only 326 yards — while the guide expects him to be asked to throw and run more with Kentrell Bullock gone.
South Alabama Jaguars.scheme_fit: Applewhite will serve as his own offensive coordinator, and the guide expects more tempo to use the receivers' speed.
South Alabama Jaguars.supporting_cast: Diminished. 1,000-yard rusher Kentrell Bullock and receiver Devin Voisin, whose 67 catches were 27 more than anyone else, are gone. Returning production is modest: Keenan Phillips at 4.8 yards per carry on 126 attempts, PJ Martin at 5.4, and Anthony Eager second in catches with 40 for only 339 yards. The guide states surprise that the Jaguars did not pursue portal receivers with more fervour.
South Alabama Jaguars.portal_context: A split verdict — the fourth-ranked freshman class per 247Sports alongside the second-worst transfer portal class.
South Alabama Jaguars.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 5.5 wins, described as trusting its own numbers, with a projection of 5.12 wins. It attaches an unusually strong variance warning: this is as high-variance a team as you will see in the Sun Belt. Faster tempo and explosive plays would change the story, but could also hurt a team very short on depth and very green in the secondary.
South Alabama Jaguars.outlook_dependency: Moderate. The guide expects quarterback-led improvement while taking the Under on depth, secondary inexperience and the cross-division draw.

Southern Miss Golden Eagles.status: New starter, identity undetermined — the guide asks whether there is a true QB1 on the roster and does not answer it.
Southern Miss Golden Eagles.previous_school: Ethan Hampton comes from Illinois, having previously started at Northern Illinois; Landry Lyddy and John White are holdovers.
Southern Miss Golden Eagles.career_experience: Hampton started a few games at Northern Illinois but barely played for the Illini; White played in 2024 but not last season.
Southern Miss Golden Eagles.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as counts.
Southern Miss Golden Eagles.passing: Lyddy threw for 406 yards with a 2-to-3 touchdown-to-interception ratio; Hampton's production is not addressed. Departing starter Braylon Braxton posted a 24-to-8 ratio with over 3,000 passing yards.
Southern Miss Golden Eagles.rushing: Lyddy had 12 yards on six carries.
Southern Miss Golden Eagles.turnovers: Lyddy's 2-to-3 ratio is the only figure given.
Southern Miss Golden Eagles.competition: Open among Landry Lyddy, Ethan Hampton and John White, with the guide naming no favourite. It allows the possibility Lyddy was merely stuck behind Braxton.
Southern Miss Golden Eagles.backup: The three named candidates are Lyddy, Hampton and White.
Southern Miss Golden Eagles.author_confidence: Low and deflationary. The guide notes Southern Miss threw for 266 yards per game last season, their most since 2019, and says not to expect anything like that again.
Southern Miss Golden Eagles.positive_case: The guide allows only that Lyddy may have been stuck behind Braxton.
Southern Miss Golden Eagles.concerns: Basically no returning production anywhere, quarterback included, because many players went to Memphis with Huff or wanted to play their final season for him.
Southern Miss Golden Eagles.scheme_fit: Not addressed in guide; head coach Blake Anderson was the offensive coordinator whose unit improved by 13.5 PPG and a full yard per play.
Southern Miss Golden Eagles.supporting_cast: Almost nothing. All nine players with at least 15 receptions are outside the programme, and 19 of the 20 players with at least 20 tackles are playing elsewhere or not at all.
Southern Miss Golden Eagles.portal_context: A hodgepodge of transfers and holdovers who stayed knowing jobs were available; Hampton from Illinois is the named quarterback addition.
Southern Miss Golden Eagles.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 3.5 wins, though the guide is candid that its own projection of 3.86 sits on the other side and that the -130 juice puts it broadly in line with the market. Its supporting evidence is how rarely Southern Miss is favoured — only twice — and it calls drawing James Madison and Old Dominion from the East as brutal as it gets, concluding this is not a bet but very clearly a transitional season.
Southern Miss Golden Eagles.outlook_dependency: High. The quarterback is the first position the guide interrogates in a roster it says has basically no returning production.
Southern Miss Golden Eagles.conflicts: The guide names three candidates and declines to state an expected starter, so this record carries no VSiN preseason expectation for the position.

Troy Trojans.status: Returning pair, unresolved — both 2025 starters are back and the guide states its own curiosity about how the competition resolves.
Troy Trojans.career_experience: Both Tucker Kilcrease and Goose Crowder sat behind Matthew Caldwell in 2024 and entered 2025 as 1a and 1b, flipping places depending on the day.
Troy Trojans.previous_starts: Not addressed as counts; the guide gives the sequence — Crowder won the job but was hurt in the third game, Kilcrease still started against Old Dominion on Crowder's return, then was hurt himself, and Crowder finished the season.
Troy Trojans.passing: Troy's quarterbacks posted a 20-to-11 touchdown-to-interception ratio while under duress on seemingly every dropback.
Troy Trojans.turnovers: 11 interceptions against 20 touchdown passes; Troy was exactly even in turnover margin.
Troy Trojans.competition: Genuinely open. The guide treats it as a rarity in the transfer era that two quarterbacks both stayed, and its evidence on their relative standing comes from the market: when Crowder was hurt and Kilcrease took over, the betting action indicated Kilcrease was seen as a clear downgrade.
Troy Trojans.backup: The two incumbents are Tucker Kilcrease and Goose Crowder; 6-foot-5 East Mississippi CC quarterback Rodge Waldrop is also on the roster.
Troy Trojans.author_confidence: Explicitly curious rather than settled — the guide states its own curiosity about how this plays out.
Troy Trojans.positive_case: The quarterbacks posted a 20-to-11 ratio while under constant duress, which the guide calls incredible, and health luck should improve.
Troy Trojans.concerns: Protection above all: 59 sacks allowed, which the guide verified was not a typo and was seven more than the next closest team.
Troy Trojans.scheme_fit: New coordinator Adam Austin led a Tarleton offense with five 50-point games that was the highest-scoring team at the FCS level and second only to North Texas across all of Division I.
Troy Trojans.supporting_cast: A couple of starters return on the offensive line, which the guide does not treat as automatically good news, with the portal heavily used to fill out the rest.
Troy Trojans.portal_context: A number of East Mississippi CC players are now on the roster, including quarterback Rodge Waldrop; the guide infers from the 2024-to-2025 defensive improvement that this staff is adept at finding talent in the portal.
Troy Trojans.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 6.5 wins — called juicy but considered a bet — with Over 7.5 also liked on an alt win total. Its projection is 6.86 wins. The closing case is health-based: Parker reached eight wins with a dumpster fire on the offensive line and two injured quarterbacks, the roster is better now, and it cannot imagine the health luck being that bad again.
Troy Trojans.outlook_dependency: Very high, and specifically on availability. The guide's Over is built on quarterback health luck reverting.
Troy Trojans.conflicts: The guide declines to name a starter between two returning quarterbacks, so this record carries no VSiN preseason expectation for the position.

ULM Warhawks.status: Transfer — from Houston; the guide expects him to play a lot rather than naming him the confirmed starter.
ULM Warhawks.career_experience: A three-star freshman ULM originally offered in Vincent's first year at the school.
ULM Warhawks.passing: Not addressed in guide for Carlisle. Incumbent Aidan Armenta posted a 12-to-8 touchdown-to-interception ratio; backup Landon Graves had 40 pass attempts.
ULM Warhawks.rushing: Not addressed in guide for Carlisle, who is described as a dual threat. Armenta managed only 57 net yards on 60 carries; Graves had 14 rushes.
ULM Warhawks.turnovers: Not addressed in guide for Carlisle; Armenta threw eight interceptions against 12 touchdowns.
ULM Warhawks.competition: Live. Incumbent Aidan Armenta and backup Landon Graves are both still with the programme, and the guide states its expectation rather than a settled outcome.
ULM Warhawks.author_confidence: Moderate and inferential. The guide says it fully expects Carlisle to play a lot, reasoning that his arrival is purposeful given ULM originally offered him.
ULM Warhawks.positive_case: He is a dual threat, and the guide identifies the quarterback run as central to the new coordinator's scheme — ICCC's Damarcus Creecy led that team with 723 rushing yards at 5.5 per carry.
ULM Warhawks.concerns: The incumbent's rushing production was negligible at 57 net yards on 60 carries, which is precisely what the new scheme requires.
ULM Warhawks.scheme_fit: Central. Vincent made an outside-the-box hire in Iowa Central Community College head coach Jesse Montalto, whose offense ranked fifth in the NJCAA at 38.6 PPG and fourth at 445.8 yards per game, built around the quarterback run.
ULM Warhawks.portal_context: Carlisle arrives from Houston; the guide supplies the backstory that ULM originally offered him as a three-star freshman.
ULM Warhawks.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 3.5 wins. The guide expects the offense to create more explosive plays and present a different look, but warns that if it does not click the defense will be under heavy fire — a huge worry. Its projections call for exactly 3.00 wins and make ULM an underdog in every game.
ULM Warhawks.outlook_dependency: Very high. The guide puts the pressure on Vincent's own specialism, noting ULM has scored 21 and 16.6 PPG in his two years and that he needs to find some offense or his tenure could be coming to a close.
